elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages under the Agreement or any Order Form.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that “Customer shall pay no liquidated damages” under the Agreement or any Order Form.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties under the Agreement or any Order Form.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that “Customer shall pay no ... penalties” under the Agreement or any Order Form.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer may arise only from early termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause prohibits all liquidated damages, so no liquidated amount can arise from a non-termination event. The fallback permits, but does not require, an early-termination fee.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' Fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is payable because all liquidated damages are expressly prohibited; therefore, no fee can exceed the three-month cap.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than the permitted early-termination fee may be payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The blanket prohibition on liquidated damages ensures that no additional liquidated amount is payable.

result.reason: The redline completely removes the original weekly late-payment liquidated damages and affirmatively prohibits all liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. It therefore achieves the preferred position and, as a stricter zero-liability outcome, also remains within the fallback's maximum permitted exposure. The change is confined to the targeted liquidated-damages provision and introduces no contradictory or unrelated obligation.
